title: Emerging Cross-lingual Structure in Pretrained Language Models
sections_checked: §4.1 domain match; §4.2 anchor-point ablations; §4.3 parameter-sharing ablations; Table 1
§5 discussion/conclusion and scope of shared-parameter claim
evidence_note: On bilingual MLMs transferring English to French/Russian/Chinese for XNLI, NER and dependency parsing, removing shared anchors causes modest mean changes (−1.1 XNLI, −2.4 NER, −0.9 parsing), while separating bottom six layers causes much larger losses (−22.6, −38.7, −17.8). Extra anchors help distant language pairs; domain mismatch hurts NER more. Eight-layer model/task/language scope; no claim that anchors never matter.

title: Privacy Risk in Machine Learning: Analyzing the Connection to Overfitting
sections_checked: §§2–5 formal stability/generalization and membership/attribute inference results
§6.2 membership inference; §6.3 attribute inference; §6.4 colluding training algorithm
evidence_note: Generalization error predicts membership-inference advantage in evaluated models; simple threshold attack has >.99 recall and .505/.694/.874 precision on MNIST/CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. Attribute inference succeeds on tested IWPC genomic attributes but not the Netflix movie target; a malicious colluding training construction reaches ≥.98 membership advantage on sufficiently large CNNs with small accuracy losses. Attack assumptions and selected benchmarks limit generalization.

title: Learning How to Mutate Source Code from Bug-Fixes
sections_checked: §III corpus extraction, abstraction, clustering and RNN training
§IV RQ1–RQ3 evaluation and Table II prediction classes
evidence_note: From 787,178 mined bug-fixing commits / ~2.3M transformation pairs, 80/10/10 train/validation/test: exact buggy-code reconstruction is 9–45% model-dependent; syntactic correctness is high, but bad predictions remain common for some models. Manual behavioral judgments inspect methods in isolation; scope is Java and mostly ≤50-token methods.

title: Proximal Operators for Multi-Agent Path Planning
sections_checked: §5 Java numerical experiments: CONF1 scaling, restarts, and landmark scenarios
§6 conclusion and Appendix A trajectory approximation
evidence_note: Synthetic numerical evaluation reports ~2× speedup with eight cores and stable-looking objective values over 1,000 initializations for a 3D CONF1 scenario; landmark examples include two-agent toys and a 10-agent/100-landmark demonstration. Authors acknowledge local minima; no real-hardware validation or global-optimum guarantee.
